001package dayplanner;
002
003
004
005import java.time.LocalTime;
006
007
008
009/**
010 * Provides shared helpers for activity category parsing, greeting generation,
011 * and search filtering. Methods are static so callers can use them without
012 * creating a utility instance.
013 */
014public class DayPlannerUtils {
015    /**
016     * Generates a multi-line time-appropriate greeting and activity summary for the
017     * user. Each line of the greeting is indented by 1 tab.
018     * 
019     * @param numActivities The current number of activities.
020     * @return Formatted greeting string indented by 1 tab.
021     */
022    public static String getGreeting(int numActivities) {
023        int hour = LocalTime.now().getHour();
024        String greeting;
025
026        if (hour < 12)      greeting = "Good morning";
027        else if (hour < 17) greeting = "Good afternoon";
028        else                greeting = "Good evening";
029
030        String text = "\t%s!\n\tYou have %d activities currently entered.";
031        return String.format(text, greeting, numActivities);
032    }
033
034
035
036    /**
037     * <p>
038     * Determines whether an activity satisfies the specified search criteria.
039     * </p>
040     * <p>
041     * All non-null criteria must be satisfied simultaneously:
042     * </p>
043     * <ul>
044     * <li><b>searchStart</b>: the activity's start time must be &gt;=
045     * <code>searchStart</code>.</li>
046     * <li><b>searchEnd</b>: the activity's end time must be &lt;=
047     * <code>searchEnd</code>.</li>
048     * </ul>
049     * <p>
050     * Passing <code>null</code> for any filter disables that filter entirely.
051     * </p>
052     * 
053     * @param act         The activity to test.
054     * @param type        If valid {@link dayplanner.ActivityType}, then
055     *                    <code>act</code> must be an instance of this type. Value
056     *                    of <code>null</code> indicates to not filter by type.
057     * @param searchStart Minimum start time, or <code>null</code> for open start.
058     * @param searchEnd   Maximum end time, or <code>null</code> for open end.
059     * @return <code>true</code> if the activity satisfies all given criteria,
060     *         <code>false</code> otherwise.
061     */
062    public static boolean matchesCriteria(Activity act, ActivityType type, Time searchStart, Time searchEnd) {
063        // if no activity was given, there is nothing to check
064        if (act == null)
065            return false;
066
067        // check type
068        if (type != null && !act.getType().equals(type))
069            return false;
070
071        // check start time
072        // a must start on or after the lower bound
073        if (searchStart != null && act.getStartTime().compareTo(searchStart) < 0)
074            return false;
075
076        // check end time
077        // a must end on or before the upper bound
078        if (searchEnd != null && act.getEndTime().compareTo(searchEnd) > 0)
079            return false;
080
081        return true;
082    }
083    
084
085    
086    /**
087     * Prompts the user for a time period filter and parses the start and end times.
088     * A blank response means both bounds are open; a single hyphen may introduce
089     * either one-sided range, for example {@code 2026/09/12 06:00 -}.
090     * 
091     * @param keyboard Input instance to use to prompt the user
092     * @return A two-element array {@code {searchStart, searchEnd}}; either element
093     *         may be null to represent an open bound.
094     */
095    public static Time[] readTimePeriod(Input keyboard) {
096        System.out.println("Enter a time period (e.g. '2026/9/12, 6:00 - 2026/9/22, 11:59', '2026/9/12, 6:00 -', '- 2026/9/22, 11:59'), or press Enter for any time:");
097        String line = keyboard.readString();
098
099        // if the user typed nothing, both sides of the range should be unrestricted
100        if (line.isEmpty())
101            return new Time[] { null, null };
102
103        // find at what index the dash is typed
104        // all common dash characters are accepted
105        int dashIndex = -1;
106        char[] dashes = { '-', '–', '—' };
107        for (char d : dashes) {
108            dashIndex = line.indexOf(d);
109            if (dashIndex != -1)
110                break;
111        }
112
113        // if the user actually did type a dash...
114        if (dashIndex != -1) {
115            // convert the input into two time instances
116            String part1 = line.substring(0, dashIndex).trim();
117            String part2 = line.substring(dashIndex + 1).trim();
118            Time start = part1.isEmpty() ? null : Input.parseTime(part1);
119            Time end = part2.isEmpty() ? null : Input.parseTime(part2);
120
121            // and only parse a boundary if the user typed one properly
122            if (!part1.isEmpty() && start == null) {
123                System.out.println("Invalid starting time. Use format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM. Try again:");
124                return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
125            }
126            if (!part2.isEmpty() && end == null) {
127                System.out.println("Invalid ending time. Use format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM. Try again:");
128                return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
129            }
130
131            // ensure that start comes first
132            if (start != null && end != null && start.compareTo(end) >= 0) {
133                System.out.println("Starting time must be before ending time. Try again:");
134                return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
135            }
136
137            return new Time[] { start, end };
138        }
139
140        // if the user didn't input a dash...
141        // then a single valid time is treated as the lower bound with no upper bound
142        Time single = Input.parseTime(line);
143        if (single != null)
144            return new Time[] { single, null };
145
146        // if we got here then nothing else worked
147        System.out.println("Invalid time period. Expected 'start - end', 'start -', '- end', or press Enter to skip. Try again:");
148        return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
149    }
150
151
152
153    /**
154     * Default constructor for DayPlannerUtils.
155     */
156    private DayPlannerUtils() {}
157}
